data.title: Binance News Update | Binance Co-CEOs Say 80% of the $6.3 Billion Loss Is Already Covered, With Withdrawals Restarting in Phases and Proof of Reserves Due Monday
data.description: Binance co-CEOs Yi He and Richard Teng said the exchange has already covered about 80% of the roughly $6.3 billion lost in its security incident and will absorb the full cost itself. In a letter to users dated Friday, October 30, they said Binance’s hot wallets were compromised at about 20:05 UTC on October 29.“Binance will absorb the financial impact of these stolen funds, not our users,” they wrote.About 80% Already CoveredBinance will cover all stolen funds through its Secure Asset Fund for Users (SAFU) and its corporate treasury, the co-CEOs said. The exchange has set aside more than $6.34 billion, $5 billion of which is held in the exact tokens that were stolen, including USDC, USDT, BTC, ETH and BNB. That covers about 80% of the loss, and Binance is buying the remaining tokens through market and over-the-counter channels.What Binance Has Done So FarSince identifying the incident, Binance has:Contained the compromised infrastructure, revoked affected authorizations and added controls to prevent further unauthorized activity.Frozen about $3 billion on-chain with help from law enforcement, blockchain intelligence firms, asset issuers and industry partners.Strengthened security checks across affected systems.Paused withdrawals for security reviews, while keeping deposits and other unaffected services running.What the Investigation Has FoundBinance’s initial investigation pointed to a compromised laptop, and further work has uncovered additional points of breach. The exchange said it has found no evidence that wallet private keys were leaked. It is working with internal and external security experts to map the full attack sequence and expects to share further verified technical findings in about 48 hours.Withdrawals and Proof of ReservesBinance said in Friday’s letter that it aimed to start resuming withdrawals within about 34 hours, in phases, once security checks are complete. It also planned an initial Proof of Reserves snapshot within 12 hours, with results by Monday, November 2, so users can verify their balances and how they are backed.The exchange will also publish a post-mortem report covering what happened, lessons learned and new safeguards. “We take full responsibility for addressing this security incident, strengthening our security infrastructure, and ensuring our users are protected,” the co-CEOs wrote.

data.title: STOCKS | Earnings-Season Selloffs Intensify for Companies Missing Estimates
data.description: U.S. stocks are seeing some of the harshest post-earnings selloffs on record for companies that miss expectations, as investors grow more sensitive to slowing profit growth. According to Sina Finance, Amazon plunged on Friday after its earnings report, while Alphabet fell by a record amount on Thursday following disappointing results; selloffs in communication services stocks that miss estimates have been the steepest since data collection began in 2019, with a similar pattern in heavyweight technology stocks. With earnings season about one-third complete, S&P 500 companies’ earnings growth has slowed to about 26%, from 32% in the second quarter. Strategists at Wells Fargo and Franklin Templeton have warned in recent weeks that higher interest rates, trade-tariff pressures, and elevated oil prices could slow earnings growth. Industry research data cited in the report put third-quarter technology earnings growth at 65%, down from nearly 77% in the prior quarter, and communication services growth at 3.2%, down from nearly 10%. Technology and communication services were the only sectors to fall this month, while all other sectors rose. Northlight Asset Management Chief Investment Officer Chris Zaccarelli said the market is more sensitive than usual and investors would rather sell first than risk further losses. Truist Advisory Services Chief Investment Officer and Chief Market Strategist Keith Lerner said the two sectors make up half the market, leading investors to demand more evidence that the trade remains viable; he added that slower growth challenges that narrative. Bokeh Capital Partners Chief Investment Officer Kimberly Forrest said investors are trimming some of technology stocks’ prior excess gains and buying cheaper stocks in other areas rather than leaving the market entirely. Overall earnings are still expected to grow: industry research estimates put S&P 500 earnings growth closer to 20% during 2027 and into the first quarter of 2028. Franklin Templeton Institute Chief Investment Strategist Jeff Schulze said that would exceed the historical 10% threshold associated with further market gains after earnings growth peaks, and that the S&P 500 could return high single digits to low double digits in 2027 if earnings meet expectations. So far, the share of S&P 500 companies beating Wall Street estimates is at its lowest level this year, including in technology, consumer discretionary, and financials. Zaccarelli said earnings misses in one area could prompt rapid repricing across related areas.

data.title: STOCKS | Nasdaq 100 Risks Technical Correction as AI Trades Unwind Rapidly
data.description: The Nasdaq 100 briefly fell 4.5% on Friday, putting it at risk of entering a technical correction. According to Sina Finance, the index fell below 28,102.2, a level 10% below its recent high; a drop below that threshold meets the definition of a technical correction. This would be the index’s third decline of at least 10% this year. Selling was driven mainly by disappointing third-quarter results at technology companies, while the rapid unwinding of AI trades also weighed on the index.

data.title: Ukraine’s Foreign Ministry: Russia-U.S.-Ukraine Talks Planned for November, Date Not Set
data.description: Ukraine is preparing for trilateral talks with negotiating teams from the United States and Russia in Abu Dhabi in November, but the date has not been set. According to Sina Finance, Foreign Ministry spokesperson Heorhiy Tykhyi said in Kyiv on Friday that the talks are expected to address security guarantees and de-escalation measures, including the situation in the Black Sea. Tykhyi said Kyiv views the Abu Dhabi talks as an opportunity to prepare for a meeting of leaders.

data.title: Trump Administration Again Loses Bid to Block California From Counting Alleged Noncitizen Votes
data.description: According to CNBC, the 9th U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals on Friday rejected the Trump administration’s request to temporarily bar California from counting mail ballots for the November 3 midterm elections cast by more than 20,000 registered voters it alleges are likely noncitizens. The 2-1 decision was the second time this week the court denied an emergency request in the case. The judges cited a lower court’s finding that the administration’s list may not be fully reliable and said granting the request could disenfranchise voters. The Justice Department filed the lawsuit on October 15. A federal judge denied its request for a temporary restraining order on October 28.

data.title: Hedge Funds’ US Natural Gas Shorts Reach Record on Warm-Winter Bets
data.description: Hedge funds amassed their largest-ever short position in US natural gas this week, betting an unusually warm winter will cut demand for the fuel used by furnaces and power plants, according to Bloomberg.

data.title: JPMorgan: U.S. Treasury Bill Demand May Not Keep Pace With 2027 Supply
data.description:
JPMorgan strategists Jay Barry, Pankaj Vohra and others said U.S. Treasury bill issuance is expected to keep expanding, with the market needing to absorb $991 billion in net supply in 2027, making demand’s ability to keep pace a key question. According to Sina Finance, the strategists see some headwinds: They expect money market fund assets under management to grow at roughly the pace seen during the larger inflows in 2024 or 2025, unless a major market disruption comparable to the 2020 pandemic shock or 2023 regional banking stress occurs.

The strategists said foreign official investors’ recent pullback has been tactical rather than structural, leaving room for them to resume a steadier pace of short-term Treasury purchases. They said a similar recovery is unlikely in the stablecoin sector unless cryptocurrencies rebound or the regulatory environment becomes clearer. Treasury bill valuations are unlikely to reverse sharply to more expensive levels next year, and pressure may be particularly evident during the 2027 supply increase as money markets absorb the additional bills and demand may grow more slowly than in previous years.

The strategists said lower bill valuations could also affect funding markets, particularly if money market funds sharply reduce repo allocations to buy more bills or funding markets become more sensitive to bill settlement dates. The debt ceiling could begin to factor in next spring, when the U.S. Treasury may reduce its general account balance, making funding market conditions harder to assess. Money market fund assets under management have stalled over the past two months. Although the strategists expect a seasonal rebound during the rest of 2026, they project growth of only about 5% for the year, compared with double-digit growth in each of the previous two years.

In the four months through August, foreign investors reduced their holdings of short-term U.S. Treasuries by about $145 billion, bringing foreign official investors’ share of holdings to 4.3%, its lowest level since May 2024. Stablecoin growth has also stalled this year. Fiat-backed stablecoin supply has fluctuated between $265 billion and $280 billion, while stablecoin holdings of Treasury bills total $127 billion, or 2% of all Treasury bills, down from $137 billion in December 2025.

data.title: Nationwide and MFS Funds Face Large Capital Gains Distributions in 2026
data.description: According to CNBC, the Nationwide Renaissance Small Cap Growth Fund (NWGPX) is estimated to distribute 56.6% of its net asset value in capital gains, while the A-share version of the MFS Global Equity Fund (MWEFX) is set to distribute 31% to 33%. Morningstar senior manager research analyst Stephen Welch compiled a list of funds with the highest estimated distributions for 2026. Fund families expect to make the distributions in December. Investors holding the funds in taxable brokerage accounts may owe long-term capital gains taxes at rates of 0%, 15% or 20%, depending on taxable income; holdings in tax-deferred accounts such as IRAs and 401(k)s are not affected. Investors can use tax-loss harvesting to offset capital gains, and may direct distributions to cash rather than reinvesting them.

data.title: STOCKS | TSX Posts Steepest Drop Since June in North American Retreat
data.description: The TSX had its sharpest decline since June as technology and materials stocks weighed on the benchmark, joining a broader North American retreat, according to Bloomberg.

data.title: STOCKS | Apple Regains World's Highest Valuation, Surpassing Nvidia
data.description: Apple reclaimed its position as the world's most valuable company on Friday, overtaking Nvidia as investors sought the perceived safety of the iPhone maker amid concerns about artificial intelligence spending, according to Bloomberg.

data.title: AstraZeneca Shares Jump Nearly 7% on Earnings Beat and $1.5 Billion Savings Plan
data.description: AstraZeneca shares rose nearly 7% on Friday after beating third-quarter earnings forecasts and announcing a restructuring plan. Third-quarter revenue rose 7% to $16.21 billion and core earnings were $2.79 per share, above the $2.59 estimate, according to BeInCrypto. Oncology revenue rose 17%, while Farxiga sales fell 25% amid generic competition; a breast cancer trial missed its main target and a lung cancer study was stopped. The plan targets $1.5 billion in annual savings, with up to $2 billion in upfront costs, for a pipeline of more than 180 projects. AstraZeneca acquired Modella AI and partnered with insitro; CEO Pascal Soriot targets $80 billion in annual revenue by 2030. Shares closed above £131.34, with chart targets of £145.38 and £157.30.
